findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed milkshake machine to be soiled with old food matter. PIC informed that a shake was just made. The current process for the milkshake machine is to clean the mixer attachment with clean water between uses, and clean/sanitize at the end of each day. Since the ice cream milk contacting the mixer attachment is a time/temperature for safety (TCS) food, the mixer attachment needs to be sanitized at minimum every four hours. Water is not an adequate form of sanitization. The mixer attachment needs to be submerged in sanitizer and air-dried to properly sanitize. PIC properly sanitized mixer attachment during the inspection. Ensure staff are sanitizing the attachment at least every four hours during use.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.11(C) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (C) Except as specified in (D) of this section, if used with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD, EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

findings.comment: Observed in use utensils in an empty pan with no time control concept. Decide on policy for storage of in use utensils. The utensils were removed to dish and replaced. 3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment: 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D)  (C) Clean Equipment/Utensils/Linens/Single-Use Articles stored incorrectly, soiled or in soiled container. Equipment, Utensils, Linens and Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D). Stote utensils clean and protected. If utensils are not used as indicated. Store utensils in such a way that it is clear they are not or remove from faciliy if not used. Utensils were moved. Bucket with other utensils was moved to dish.

findings.comment: Cookies made in house and wrapped do not have a label. 750-110g Every food pre-packaged in advance of retail sale must bear the following information in English on its label: common name;, address, zip code of the manufacturer, processor, packer, preparer, or distributor; net contents of package; a list of ingredients by their common or usual name; and a list of any artificial color, flavor, or preservative used. findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750.830g - Quat test strips were observed to be water damaged. Another set of strips were obtained from the mobile unit parked out back, and those strips were also water damaged. Manager noted the owner was contacted and would purchase a new set prior to arriving at the facility today.

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Sanitizer solution was prepared for wiping surfaces and was observed to be below 200ppm quat. Manger noted only a half a pump from the wall mounted chemical dispeser was added to the solution because she was concerned a whole pump of the chemical would be too much. More sanitizer was added to bring the solution to proper concentration of 200ppm.

Maintain sanitizer solutions at 200ppm, and use test strips to verify concentration is correct.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text:
750.1060 - Hot water does not shut off at the 3 part sink faucet when the water is set to free flow from the faucet. The only way to "shut off" the water is to switch the lever between free flowing and use of the sprayer. Repair the faucet at the 3 part sink so the water shuts off at both the cold and hot water handles when the faucet is set to free flowing.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Employee was wiping down general surfaces with a wiping cloth but container of sanitizer solution was not available for rinsing/storing the wiping cloth. Employee stated the sanitizer solution was emptied just prior to the inspector arriving to the facility. Employee was advised on proper storage and use of wet wiping cloths. Sanitizer solution was prepared for use (200ppm quat).

If surfaces are being wiped down, then a container of sanitizer solution must be maintained for rinsing wiping cloths during continuous use and storage between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) can opener blade (food debris) - set aside at dish area to be cleaned and sanitized during inspection; 
B) hood baffles (grease buildup);   and
C) hotdog pan in bottom of large prep cooler (buildup) - pan was placed in dish area to be cleaned and sanitized during inspection.

To prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris, clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed, up to every 4hrs after continuous use for in-use equipment such as can openers, knifes, cutting boards, etc.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 & 250 - A) 1. Hotdogs in bottom of prep cooler did not have date mark. Management noted hotdogs were prepped about 2 days ago. Benefit of doubt was given. Hotdogs were dated and kept for use.
2. Chili in walkin cooler had prep date of 12/28. Management stated the chili was old and was going to be discarded. The chili in question was not used for service today. Chili in the steam table was obtained from the Chadito's North location.
3. Fish sauce in the walkin cooler was dated 12/24. Management thought the sauce was made on 12/31 and just dated incorrectly. Sauce was discarded.

Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly date and consumed,  sold, or discarded within 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

B) Portions of fish sauce and sour cream in the top holding area of the large prep cooler had internal temperatures of 45F/46F and 47F/48F. Portions were located on top of a lid and were not down in a container in the holding area. Portions were discarded in the trash.

Cold potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41F/below while on display and service. **Be careful with portions and containers in prep coolers. Items stacked above the holding area in the top of the cooler will not be in direct contact with the cold air and are likely to creep into the temperature danger zone above 41F**

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
750.650a - A) Blade of can opener was showing signs of wear. Pits have formed in a few places along edges. Replace the can opener blade.
B) Baffle inside ice machine was soiled and needs to be cleaned and sanitized. Parts of the baffle were starting to show signs of wear. Grooves/pits were felt in several spots. Re-surface (sand down the baffle to allow for smooth/easily cleanable surface) or replace the baffle in the ice machine.

Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text:
750.690 - Shelving in the walkin cooler was soiled with mold growth in several spots. The shelving on the right side also had chipping paint. Clean and re-paint the shelves in the walkin cooler.

Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Spray bottle of bleach solution tested at 0ppm. Solution was remade to be at proper concentration (200ppm).

Maintain bleach solutions in spray bottle at 100-200ppm. Use test strips to verify concentration, and change out solutions in bottles daily/as needed.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Chili and cheese sauce prepared this afternoon were observed cooling in the walkin cooler. The date was noted but the time at which the cooling process began was not documented. GM wrote time on the labels. Both products were still within the first 2 hours of the cooling process. 

Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41F.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.820 - Sanitizer concentration at 3 part sink was at 100ppm quat during ware washing process. Employee doing dishes noted some very greasy pans just went through ware washing process. Water was emptied, sink was cleaned, and solution was remade to be at proper concentration of 200ppm.
Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4). Maintain quat solution at 200ppm. Monitor the sanitizer solution during ware washing and change as needed to ensure all equipment and utensils are being properly sanitized.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750.510d - Owner turned off the manual faucet prior to drying hands with a paper towel after handwashing process was completed. Proper handwashing technique and use of gloves was discussed extensively during the inspection. Hands were re-washed with proper technique, and paper towel that was used to dry hands was then used to turn off the manual faucet. To avoid re-contaminating hands after handwashing process is completed always use paper towels to turn off the faucet.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: 750.830g - Chlorine test strips were not available for bleach water solutions. Obtain and use chlorine test strips to verify bleach solutions are maintained at proper concentration. A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of each chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solutions in parts per million. **If solutions are too weak they are not sanitizing, and if they are too strong they are toxic. The only way to know the concentration is to use test strips. Maintain spray bottles of bleach water at 100ppm.**

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text: 750.1300 & 1320b - Spray bottle hanging on the dirty dish/chemical cart was not labeled. Owner noted it was supposed to be bleach water. The solution tested out as almost straight bleach (test strip stayed mostly white/had purple edge). Chemical was discarded down the mopsink. Chemicals shall not be used in any way that may contaminate food, equipment/utensils, nor in any way that constitutes a hazard to people. Containers/spray bottles of chemicals and chemical solutions (i.e. bleach water, quat solutions) must be properly labeled. Maintain bleach solutions at 100ppm and properly label spray bottles as to the chemical contents.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: 750.140b  - Cooling cheese sauce in lower section of back prep cooler was labeled as to date but no time was indicated. Product was still within the first 2hrs of cooling process and placed in an ice bath to finish rapidly cooling. Owner was advised on monitoring time and temperature during cooling process and noting the time on the label so as to avoid confusion in the future. Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41F/below.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.
